author: Barton, Craig

summary: This page summarises Kuepper-Tetzel and Gardner's two-experiment investigation into temporarily withholding grades so students engage with written feedback before seeing a numerical mark. One study was a randomized controlled trial, the other quasi-experimental; both compared students given feedback-before-grade against students given grade-first. Across both designs, delaying grade release consistently improved performance on subsequent assessments, with the effect strongest for lower-achieving students, and the improvement appears to be driven by increased engagement with the feedback itself rather than the delay alone. Barton frames this as a low-cost, easily adopted classroom practice: teachers can simply withhold the numerical grade for a short period while students first work through the written feedback, and can boost buy-in by explaining the rationale, managing expectations, and building in short reflective activities such as written responses to the feedback before the grade is revealed.
points: Temporarily withholding the grade so students engage with written feedback first consistently improved performance on later assessments across two separate experiments.
The benefit was strongest for low-achieving students, who otherwise might disengage from feedback once a grade is visible.
The effect appears to be driven by increased feedback engagement rather than the delay itself, though the precise mechanism needs more research.
This is a low-cost intervention: teachers can implement it by explaining the rationale, managing expectations, and adding brief reflection activities before revealing the grade.
quotes: In conclusion, our findings show positive effects of temporary mark withholding on report performance in psychology for Year 2 and Year 3 students. This converging finding from two experiments is particularly compelling because it was: (a) revealed in an authentic educational setting that captured student learning as it unfolds; and (b) obtained by using different methodological approaches in each of the experiments
The results consistently showed that delaying grade release led to improved performance on subsequent assessments, particularly for low-achieving students
This positive effect is linked to increased feedback engagement, although the precise mediating mechanisms require further exploration
Temporary mark withholding is a low-cost teaching practice that can easily be implemented by instructors
Teachers should openly discuss the rationale behind the approach, manage student expectations, and design short activities such as written reflection statements or questions about feedback
